content.text:
@skills/whatsapp/scripts/whatsapp.py 

The CLI has no contacts capability at all. The only way to resolve "send
 to Mistura" → a JID today is:

 1. chats — lists recent chats with their display names. No search param,
    fixed limit, and truncated name columns.
 2. The agent greps that output and guesses the JID.

 That's exactly how the Mistura send went: grep for "mistura" → nothing,
 because her saved chat name is "Misty" (a self-set nickname, not your
 address-book name). I recovered by eyeballing the list and inferring it
 was her.

 The ironic part: ruwa does expose a contacts endpoint — I just confirmed
 it's live:

 ```
   GET /v1/sessions/:id/contacts
   →
 [{"jid":"...@s.whatsapp.net","full_name":null,"push_name":"Misty","busines
 s_name":null}, ...]
 ```

 The CLI just never wraps it. So this is a gap in the skill, not a protocol
 limitation.

 The proposal

 Add contacts search <query>: fetch the contacts list, fuzzy-match across
 push_name / full_name / business_name / JID digits, then:
 - unambiguous match → return the JID (the agent can send immediately)
 - multiple hits → print a candidate table and let the agent/user pick

 ~40 lines, endpoint already works.

 Trade-offs

 1. Push names ≠ address-book names (the big one). WhatsApp Web's protocol
 doesn't sync your address book — ruwa's own SPEC notes contact app-state
 sync hasn't landed (full_name is null for everyone). So push_name is
 whatever the contact set themselves: nicknames, emojis, "Samiratou Georges
 Beber". Searching "Mistura Bebert" may still fail on the same contact that
 caused this problem. Fuzzy matching (substrings, token overlap, number
 match) narrows but doesn't eliminate the miss. Honest framing: this makes
 lookups better, not infallible.

 2. Ambiguity vs. autonomy. "Send to Misty" with two Mistys in the list —
 do we auto-pick or ask? Auto-pick risks messaging the wrong person, which
 is irreversible and socially awkward. Asking every time negates the
 convenience. My suggestion: exact unique match → send; multiple/fuzzy
 matches → always surface candidates. Slightly more friction, much safer.

 3. JID types. The contacts list mixes @s.whatsapp.net (phone) and @lid
 (WhatsApp's newer linked-device IDs, e.g. Joel above). Matching must
 prefer phone JIDs or resolve LID↔phone, or a "found" contact could be one
 the send path handles poorly.

 4. Scale. The endpoint returns the full contact list (hundreds of rows)
 per query. Fine client-side, but it's an unauthenticated-to-your-contacts
 dump every search — irrelevant locally, worth knowing if this ever moves
 to a shared server.

 5. The simpler alternative. Instead of a new subcommand, add a --search
 filter to the existing chats command. Covers ~90% of cases (you message
 people you've messaged), zero new surface — but fails exactly where you'd
 notice: contacts with old/no chat history, and it inherits the chat-list's
 name data rather than the fuller contacts table.

 My take: do contacts search as proposed (endpoint's free, ruwa supports
 it), with conservative ambiguity behavior. Want me to build it?

# WhatsApp (ruwa) Skill

Use this skill to send WhatsApp messages and inspect a [ruwa](https://github.com/oqva-digital/ruwa) instance from the terminal. All operations go through the ruwa HTTP API; this skill wraps it in a small `uv` inline-script CLI so the agent doesn't hand-roll `curl` + bearer headers + session IDs every time.

## Setup (once)

`uv` must be on PATH (managed via `mise`). Then ensure the env vars are exported in the shell the agent runs in:

```sh
export RUWA_API_ENDPOINT=https://<endpoint>   # scheme-less host is fine too
export RUWA_API_TOKEN=<bearer token>                    # ruwa admin token
export RUWA_SESSION=<session>                                  # optional: session id or label
```

Verify connectivity:

```sh
./scripts/whatsapp.py health
# status:   ok  version: 0.3.5
```

The script (`scripts/whatsapp.py`, resolved relative to this skill directory) is a PEP-723 inline script — `uv` installs its single dependency (`httpx`) on first run and caches it. Run it directly (the shebang invokes `uv run --script`) or explicitly via `uv run --script scripts/whatsapp.py ...`.

## Send a message

```sh
# text
./scripts/whatsapp.py send <number> "Hello from my agent"

# reply to / quote a message (1:1 shorthand)
./scripts/whatsapp.py send <number> "noted 👍" --reply-to <message_id>

# group reply (quote + participant author)
./scripts/whatsapp.py send <group_jid> "yes" --quote-id <message_id> --quote-participant <number>

# @mention (repeatable; bare phone is fine)
./scripts/whatsapp.py send <group_jid> "hey @<number>" --mention <number>

# media (local file or http URL; type/mime auto-detected)
./scripts/whatsapp.py send-media <number> ./photo.jpg --caption "look"
./scripts/whatsapp.py send-media <number> https://example.com/cat.png
```

The `to` / `chat` / `--mention` args accept either a **bare phone number** (`<number>`) or a **full jid** (`<number>@s.whatsapp.net`); bare numbers are normalized to `@s.whatsapp.net`.

On success the CLI prints `✓ sent to <n>  id=<id>  status=<queued|sent|…>`. Add `--json` for the raw API response (useful when the agent needs the message id to reply later).

## Inspect

```sh
./scripts/whatsapp.py sessions                 # list instances
./scripts/whatsapp.py chats                    # recent chats (default session)
./scripts/whatsapp.py chats --limit 20
./scripts/whatsapp.py messages <number>    # conversation with a contact
./scripts/whatsapp.py messages <number> --limit 20
```

All inspect commands accept `--json`.

## Pair a new number

```sh
./scripts/whatsapp.py qr               # pairing QR (view in the ruwa dashboard)
./scripts/whatsapp.py pair-phone <number>   # phone-link code, enter on the primary device
```

## Session selection

Every command accepts `--session <id-or-label>`; otherwise the CLI uses `RUWA_SESSION`, and if that's unset and exactly one session exists it is used automatically. `sessions` lists the known ids/labels.

## Error handling

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `HTTP 401: unauthorized` | wrong/empty token | check `RUWA_API_TOKEN` |
| `HTTP 404: not found: session` | bad session id/label | `./scripts/whatsapp.py sessions`; set `RUWA_SESSION` |
| `session 'x' not found` | label typo or session not created | list sessions; create one via the dashboard or `POST /v1/sessions` |
| `request failed: ...` | wrong endpoint / network / proxy | `health` to confirm reachability |
| send returns `queued` but never `delivered` | linked device offline / banned | check `health` for the session; re-pair if needed |

## Notes

- This speaks the **unofficial** WhatsApp Web multi-device protocol via ruwa — automating real accounts may violate WhatsApp's ToS. Prefer numbers you own.
- Outbound send latency is gated by WhatsApp's servers, not ruwa — `queued` → `sent` → `delivered` events are visible via the session's event stream (`GET /v1/sessions/:id/events/history`).
- The full HTTP API (webhooks, SSE, reactions, edits, polls, presence, S3 media, MCP) is documented in the ruwa repo's `SPEC.md`; this CLI covers the common messaging + inspection surface.

```

All inspect commands accept `--json`.

### Resolve a contact → JID

`send` needs a number or JID, but you usually only know a name. Use `contacts search`:

```sh
./scripts/whatsapp.py contacts search misty
# ✓ unique exact match: Misty  4474…@s.whatsapp.net

./scripts/whatsapp.py contacts search georges   # ambiguous → candidate table
./scripts/whatsapp.py contacts search 447470124659   # numbers work too
./scripts/whatsapp.py contacts search bebert --json  # all matches + scores
```

Behavior is deliberately conservative:

- **Unique exact name match** → prints the JID directly; send immediately.
- **Anything else** (substring, partial token, multiple hits) → prints a scored candidate table; pick the JID from it. Never guess between candidates — messaging the wrong person is irreversible.
- No match → exit 1 with an error.

Caveat: contact names are **push names** (whatever the contact set themselves), not your address-book names — ruwa doesn't sync address-book contacts (`full_name` is usually null). Searching "Mistura Bebert" can miss a contact whose push name is "Misty". If a search fails, try a shorter/different fragment, or fall back to `chats` + `messages` to identify the JID from conversation history. Phone JIDs (`@s.whatsapp.net`) are preferred over `@lid` when scores tie.

content.text:
Built, tested against the live server, and committed (`904e24b`).

## What shipped

**`skills/whatsapp/scripts/whatsapp.py`** — new `contacts` command:
- `contacts [--limit N] [--json]` — full contact list (NAME / JID / BUSINESS columns)
- `contacts search <query> [--json]` — fuzzy match across `push_name` / `full_name` / `business_name` / JID digits. Scoring: exact name 100 → prefix 80 → substring 60 → all-tokens 55 → partial token overlap → phone-number match. Ties break toward `@s.whatsapp.net` over `@lid`.

**Ambiguity policy, as you proposed**: only a *unique exact* name match resolves to a single JID line (`✓ unique exact match: Misty 4474…@s.whatsapp.net`); everything else prints a scored candidate table and exits 0 for the agent to pick explicitly. No match → exit 1.

## Live results against your 1098 contacts

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| `misty` | ✓ unique exact → `447470124659@s.whatsapp.net` — the original failure now resolves in one shot |
| `georges` | 2 candidates tabled (Georges BEBERT, Samiratou Georges Beber) — correctly refuses to guess |
| `bebert` | 1 *substring* match → still tabled, not auto-picked (conservative as designed) |
| `mistura` | no match — the push-name limitation you predicted, now stated in the error message itself |
| `a` | 736 candidates, capped at 15 rows, `--json` for all |

Docs synced: SKILL.md got a "Resolve a contact → JID" section with the exact-vs-candidate policy and the push-name caveat spelled out, plus a troubleshooting row; README skills table and frontmatter triggers updated per AGENTS.md.

One design note: I made the no-match error message carry the caveat ("names are push names set by the contact, not address-book names") so a future grep-and-guess agent sees the *why*, not just the failure — that's the Mistura case becoming self-explanatory.
